description.p: DropTerm is a cross-platform drop-down terminal in the Yakuake and Guake tradition: one keypress slides a full terminal overlay down from the top of the screen, the same keypress hides it again, and the shell session keeps running in between. It is built for every platform: COSMIC, GNOME, X11, macOS, and Windows.

It supports multiple tabs with per-tab titles, launch profiles, a light/dark theme pin with twelve built-in color schemes, a bell that surfaces as a desktop notification, and remote control over D-Bus — so a keyboard shortcut, a command, or the tray icon can all toggle the terminal.

DropTerm becomes plain dropterm: the binary, the app id, the repository, and the release assets all drop the cosmic-ext- prefix, and the configuration moves with them - settings, profiles, and keybindings now live as RON sections under ~/.config/io.github.l1br3_io.dropterm/ (config.ron, profiles.ron, keybinds.ron, and the optional completions.toml), replacing the one-file-per-key layout under the old cosmic-config directory. The move is greenfield: nothing imports the old layout, so the first start begins from the defaults. Editing the files applies live, and sessions follow the new id.

Also carries the never-published 0.4.0 payload: pasted images with a per-tab images panel, the status band's leading glyphs, hairlines, and hover tips, and always-on autosuggestion generators with a background-loaded completions table. Where the compositor offers no layer-shell protocol, the binary now names it and exits non-zero instead of silently never appearing.

Pasted images, end to end: an image on the clipboard - a screenshot tool's copy, or a file copied in COSMIC Files - is read, cached under ~/.cache/dropterm/paste/ in its own format, and its path pastes as text, while a per-tab images panel lists every paste with a thumbnail, its stamp, and its five verbs: Open, Copy path, Copy image, Re-paste, and a two-step Delete. The panel opens from the status band's new pasted-images chip, the band's context menu, or Ctrl+Shift+P. The status band also gains a leading glyph on every segment and hairlines dividing adjacent segments, with a hover tip on all of them. The autosuggestion generators are always on, their toggle removed, and the completion table loads in the background.

Fixes: copies land while the terminal is unfocused or hidden, the clipboard anchor reopens when the compositor closes it, a stay-open surface shares the keyboard instead of holding it hostage, and the images panel's armed delete fits its drawer.

Review hardening of the kitty graphics z-layers: eviction keeps the layer with the pixels, an explicit z on the wire moves an existing placement's seat, an absent z keeps what the seat already holds, and the above-glyph pass composites by z — kitty's own overlap rule.

Autosuggestions, computed entirely terminal-side with no shell integration: the rest of the most recent matching command from this tab's own history shows as dim ghost text while you type — Right accepts it, Alt+Right takes one word, and nothing runs without an explicit accept. Path tokens complete from the filesystem, command names from the spawn-time PATH snapshot, and git, cargo, docker, systemctl, and npm gain subcommand and long-flag completion; an optional idle delay holds a suggestion back until typing pauses, and every provider carries its own toggle in the settings drawer. The status band gained a command-lifecycle tier — a live duration segment, a finished-command notification, and a scrolled-back chip that jumps to the bottom on click — plus double-click to select a whole segment and middle-click paste. The settings drawer gained a font picker with every monospace family previewed in its own face, and the app now hides from the dock and window switcher by default, with a show_in_dock key to restore a presence.

Fixes: toggle-show on an empty desktop lands focused with keybinds live, the block caret paints in the first shown frame after every re-show, font zoom applies immediately, and an empty terminal title report clears the title instead of ignoring it.

New status band beneath the terminal — segments for the working path, git branch, profile, and more, with click-to-copy, text selection, and a right-click menu. The Profiles page gained explicit, transactional editing (Save/Cancel, a two-step delete, per-profile overrides), and the tab strip and status band each grew an optional hairline border.

Fixes: the window background follows the effective dark or light mode, profile commands run through the shell as a preamble, unspawnable programs degrade to a plain shell instead of a silent no-op, and every surface carries the app id so the shell never shows 'unknown'.
First release: drop-down terminal overlay, tabs and launch profiles, theming, bell notifications, D-Bus remote control, and the companion panel applet.
